title: Binary products in a mixed Grothendieck construction
statement:
Use the infinity categories, spaces and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarging the ambient universe when forming categories of categories. Write $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ for the infinity category of infinity categories and functors of the chosen size. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ have finite products and let $F:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ be a functor. Its mixed Grothendieck construction $\mathcal E$ has objects $(a,b,u)$ with $u\in F(a,b)$; the homotopy fiber over $(\alpha:a\to a',\beta:b\to b')$ of the map from $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}((a,b,u),(a',b',v))$ to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(a,a')\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,b')$ is
$$\operatorname{Map}_{F(a,b')}(F(a,\beta)u,F(\alpha,b')v),$$
with composition and all coherences induced by $F$. Here a product is characterized by its product mapping spaces. For a functor $p$, an arrow $e\to e'$ is cocartesian if for every $z$ the square $\operatorname{Map}(e',z)\to\operatorname{Map}(e,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}(pe',pz)\to\operatorname{Map}(pe,pz)$ is a homotopy pullback; a cocartesian fibration has such lifts for every arrow out of $pe$. The cartesian convention is the opposite one. Equivalently this is the orthofibration classified by $F$, cartesian in $\mathcal A$ and cocartesian in $\mathcal B$. The projection $\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ is a cocartesian fibration, with transport $(a,b,u)\mapsto(a,b',F(a,\beta)u)$. Assume each $F(a,-)$ preserves binary products: for every $b,b'$ the canonical comparison induced by the two projections, $F(a,b\times b')\to F(a,b)\times F(a,b')$, is an equivalence. Then $\mathcal E$ has binary products and both projections to $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ preserve them. The product of $(a,b,u)$ and $(a',b',v)$ lies over $(a\times a',b\times b')$ and corresponds to $(F(\pi_a,b)u,F(\pi_{a'},b')v)$ under the equivalence
$$F(a\times a',b\times b')\xrightarrow{\sim}F(a\times a',b)\times F(a\times a',b').$$

proof.text: We first state the fiberwise test used below. All fibers and pullbacks here and below are homotopy fibers and homotopy pullbacks, and all mapping spaces are Kan complexes; they fit into the enlarged universe of the statement, so the cited small-space criterion applies there. Suppose $\phi:R\to R'$ is a map of spaces lying over a map $\psi:H\to H'$ of base spaces, where $r:R\to H$ and $r':R'\to H'$ are the given maps and $r'\phi\simeq\psi r$ by a specified homotopy. By [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], if $\psi$ is an equivalence, then $\phi$ is an equivalence if and only if every induced map $\operatorname{hofib}_h(r)\to\operatorname{hofib}_{\psi(h)}(r')$, $h\in H$, is an equivalence. The cited statement allows non-fibrations, empty spaces and empty homotopy fibers, so no Kan-fibration replacement or set-theoretic fiber appears. The case $H=H'$, $\psi=\mathrm{id}$ is the test over a fixed base.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, mapping-space proof (binary products only); the argument below expands the passage from homotopy fibers to total spaces. Step 1.

proof.text: The asserted transport over $\beta:b\to b'$ is represented by the identity of $F(a,\beta)u$ in the prescribed mapping fiber over $(\mathrm{id}_a,\beta)$. To check that this arrow is cocartesian for $p_B:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$, fix $z=(c,d,v)$ and pull $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}((a,b,u),z)$ back along $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b',d)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,d)$. Compare it with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}((a,b',F(a,\beta)u),z)$. Over $(\alpha:a\to c,\gamma:b'\to d)$ the comparison is the equivalence between $\operatorname{Map}_{F(a,d)}(F(a,\gamma)F(a,\beta)u,F(\alpha,d)v)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{F(a,d)}(F(a,\gamma\beta)u,F(\alpha,d)v)$ supplied by the functorial coherence of $F$. Here $\phi$ is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}((a,b',F(a,\beta)u),z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}((a,b,u),z)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,d)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b',d)$, both over $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(a,c)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b',d)$ with $\psi=\mathrm{id}$; the fiber of the pullback over $(\alpha,\gamma)$ is the fiber of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}((a,b,u),z)$ over $(\alpha,\gamma\beta)$. The test of step 1, i.e. [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], proves the required pullback square of mapping spaces. There is such an arrow for every $\beta$, giving precisely the cocartesian lifts asserted in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, mapping-space proof (binary products only); the argument below expands the passage from homotopy fibers to total spaces. Step 2.

proof.text: Write $U=(a,b,u)$, $V=(a',b',v)$, $A=a\times a'$ and $B=b\times b'$. The assumed equivalence $C_A:F(A,B)\simeq F(A,b)\times F(A,b')$ has an inverse. Let $q\in F(A,B)$ be the inverse image of $(F(\pi_a,b)u,F(\pi_{a'},b')v)$, including the resulting two comparison equivalences, and put $Q=(A,B,q)$. The first comparison equivalence represents an arrow $Q\to U$ over $(\pi_a,\pi_b)$ by the mapping-fiber formula in the statement, since its source is $F(A,\pi_b)q$ and its target is $F(\pi_a,b)u$. The second gives $Q\to V$ over $(\pi_{a'},\pi_{b'})$. This constructs a cone with exactly the two base projection cones claimed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, mapping-space proof (binary products only); the argument below expands the passage from homotopy fibers to total spaces. Step 3.

proof.text:
Fix $x=(s,t,w)$. Composition with the two arrows just constructed defines $\Phi_x:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,Q)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,U)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,V)$. Its map on bases is an equivalence by the defining mapping-space properties of $A$ and $B$, followed by reordering the four factors. Over $\alpha:s\to A$, $\beta:t\to B$, put $\alpha_1=\pi_a\alpha$, $\alpha_2=\pi_{a'}\alpha$, $\beta_1=\pi_b\beta$, and $\beta_2=\pi_{b'}\beta$. Apply the given equivalence $C_s:F(s,B)\simeq F(s,b)\times F(s,b')$ to the mapping space
$$\operatorname{Map}_{F(s,B)}(F(s,\beta)w,F(\alpha,B)q).$$
An equivalence induces an equivalence on mapping spaces by applying its inverse and the two inverse equivalences; mapping spaces in a product category are products by definition. Hence this space becomes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{F(s,b)}(F(s,\beta_1)w,F(\alpha_1,b)u)\times\operatorname{Map}_{F(s,b')}(F(s,\beta_2)w,F(\alpha_2,b')v).$$
Here the target identifications are explicitly $F(s,\pi_b)F(\alpha,B)q\simeq F(\alpha,b)F(A,\pi_b)q\simeq F(\alpha,b)F(\pi_a,b)u\simeq F(\alpha_1,b)u$ and $F(s,\pi_{b'})F(\alpha,B)q\simeq F(\alpha,b')F(A,\pi_{b'})q\simeq F(\alpha,b')F(\pi_{a'},b')v\simeq F(\alpha_2,b')v$. The source identifications are $F(s,\pi_b)F(s,\beta)w\simeq F(s,\beta_1)w$ and $F(s,\pi_{b'})F(s,\beta)w\simeq F(s,\beta_2)w$. These chains use just the functorial coherence stipulated for $F$. Applying $F(s,\pi_b)$ and then the first target chain sends a morphism $h$ to the composite defining the first component of $\Phi_x$; the primed chain gives its second component. Thus this is the actual map induced by the cone, not merely an abstract equivalence of the two fiber spaces. The right side is exactly the product of the required two mapping fibers by the defining formula for $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, mapping-space proof (binary products only); the argument below expands the passage from homotopy fibers to total spaces. Step 4.

proof.text: Step 4 makes every homotopy-fiber map of $\Phi_x$ an equivalence over an equivalence of bases. Applying the test of step 1 with $\phi=\Phi_x$ and $\psi$ the base equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(s,A)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(t,B)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(s,a)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(t,b)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(s,a')\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(t,b')$ (the homotopy fiber of the product map over a point is the product of the two homotopy fibers), [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] proves that $\Phi_x$ is an equivalence for every $x$. The defining product mapping-space property therefore proves that $Q$ with the specified cone is a binary product. Its images are the specified product cones $A\to a,a'$ and $B\to b,b'$, so each projection preserves binary products. The construction applies to every pair $U,V$; no terminal-object comparison $F(a,1_{\mathcal B})\simeq *$ was used or claimed.
